Constraint.headline: Inconsistent financial results
Constraint.description: Profit margin and cash flow are unpredictable, making it hard to plan, finance, or eventually sell the business.
Constraint.priorityAction: Review your pricing and margins this month, and identify one way to make next month's revenue more predictable.
Constraint.priorityWhyItMatters: Predictable profit and cash flow directly increase what the business is worth and reduce financial stress on you personally.

Developing.headline: Financial results are improving but still inconsistent
Developing.description: You have some profit and revenue predictability, but not enough yet to plan with confidence.
Developing.priorityAction: Identify the single biggest source of margin leakage or revenue unpredictability and address it this quarter.
Developing.priorityWhyItMatters: Closing the gap between 'somewhat predictable' and 'reliable' meaningfully increases what the business is worth.

Solid.headline: Your financial foundation is solid
Solid.description: Profit and revenue are reasonably predictable — there's room to make them more resilient.
Solid.priorityAction: Build a rolling 90-day cash flow forecast so you can see disruptions coming instead of reacting to them.
Solid.priorityWhyItMatters: Forecasting turns a solid financial position into a genuinely resilient one.

Strength.headline: Your financial foundation is strong
Strength.description: Strong, predictable margins give you real options — to reinvest, to plan ahead, and to negotiate from strength.
Strength.priorityAction: Set a formal capital allocation plan (reinvest, reserve, distribute) and stress-test it against a revenue downturn.
Strength.priorityWhyItMatters: Protecting and deliberately allocating a strong financial position compounds the advantage instead of letting it drift.

Constraint.headline: Inconsistent execution
Constraint.description: Without documented processes, quality and output depend entirely on who happens to be doing the work.
Constraint.priorityAction: Document your top two recurring processes as simple step-by-step guides this quarter.
Constraint.priorityWhyItMatters: Documented processes let the business run consistently without depending on any one person, including you.

Developing.headline: Execution is becoming more consistent
Developing.description: Some processes are documented, but quality still varies depending on who's doing the work.
Developing.priorityAction: Pick the process most prone to inconsistency and document it well enough that someone new could follow it.
Developing.priorityWhyItMatters: Each process you document reduces how much quality depends on any one person.

Solid.headline: Your operations run fairly consistently
Solid.description: Most key processes are documented — the next step is making sure they're actually followed and effective.
Solid.priorityAction: Set one measurable quality or output metric for your most important process and start tracking it monthly.
Solid.priorityWhyItMatters: Measuring a documented process is what turns 'documented' into 'reliable'.

Strength.headline: Your operations run consistently
Strength.description: Documented, repeatable processes mean quality doesn't depend on any one person — including you.
Strength.priorityAction: Identify the one remaining bottleneck that still routes through you personally, and hand it off.
Strength.priorityWhyItMatters: Removing the last few owner-dependent steps protects consistency as the business grows.

Constraint.headline: Unclear path to growth
Constraint.description: Without a repeatable way to attract customers, growth is unpredictable and hard to plan around.
Constraint.priorityAction: Identify the one marketing or sales activity that has worked best, and turn it into a repeatable process.
Constraint.priorityWhyItMatters: A repeatable growth engine makes future revenue less dependent on luck or one-off effort.

Developing.headline: You have the beginnings of a growth engine
Developing.description: Something is working some of the time, but it's not yet reliable enough to plan around.
Developing.priorityAction: Track where your last five customers actually came from, and double down on whichever source shows up more than once.
Developing.priorityWhyItMatters: Knowing what's actually working — not just what you assume is working — is the fastest way to make growth repeatable.

Solid.headline: You have a reasonably repeatable path to growth
Solid.description: Demand generation works more often than not — there's room to make it more predictable.
Solid.priorityAction: Set a simple monthly target for your best-performing growth channel and track it against actuals.
Solid.priorityWhyItMatters: Targets turn 'usually works' into a plannable, forecastable growth engine.

Strength.headline: You have a repeatable path to growth
Strength.description: A reliable way to bring in new customers makes future growth less dependent on luck or one-off effort.
Strength.priorityAction: Test whether your growth engine can scale — increase spend or effort on your best channel and measure the response.
Strength.priorityWhyItMatters: Confirming your growth engine scales (not just works) is what compounds business value over time.

Constraint.headline: The business depends heavily on you
Constraint.description: If the business can't run well without you, it limits your freedom and is worth less to a future buyer.
Constraint.priorityAction: Hand off one customer or vendor relationship you currently manage personally to a team member this month.
Constraint.priorityWhyItMatters: Every relationship that moves off your desk gives you more freedom and makes the business less dependent on you.

Developing.headline: The business is becoming less dependent on you
Developing.description: Some relationships and decisions no longer require you personally, but many still do.
Developing.priorityAction: List every decision that currently requires your sign-off, and delegate the one that's easiest to hand off.
Developing.priorityWhyItMatters: Each decision you delegate is a small, compounding increase in both your freedom and the business's value.

Solid.headline: The business runs reasonably well without you
Solid.description: Most key relationships and decisions don't strictly require you — a few still do.
Solid.priorityAction: Take a real, unplugged two-day break and note exactly what needed you. Fix that gap.
Solid.priorityWhyItMatters: A short test run surfaces the remaining dependencies before a real absence forces the issue.

Strength.headline: The business doesn't depend entirely on you
Strength.description: Key relationships and decisions that don't run through you personally give you real freedom and make the business more valuable to a future buyer.
Strength.priorityAction: Formally document decision authority for your team so independence survives turnover, not just your current staff.
Strength.priorityWhyItMatters: Freedom that depends on specific people isn't durable — documenting it protects the value you've built.

Constraint.headline: Limited ability to absorb setbacks
Constraint.description: Without a financial or operational cushion, a single setback can put the business in real jeopardy.
Constraint.priorityAction: Set a target cash reserve and start setting aside a fixed amount each month until you reach it.
Constraint.priorityWhyItMatters: A cash reserve protects the business's value and gives you the freedom to weather a setback without panic.

Developing.headline: You have some ability to absorb a setback
Developing.description: You could handle a minor disruption, but a serious one would still hurt badly.
Developing.priorityAction: Estimate how many weeks of expenses your current reserve would cover, and set a target to double it.
Developing.priorityWhyItMatters: Knowing your actual runway turns a vague sense of risk into a concrete, trackable goal.

Solid.headline: You're reasonably prepared to absorb setbacks
Solid.description: You have a real cushion — stress-testing it against a specific scenario would confirm how far it goes.
Solid.priorityAction: Walk through what would actually happen if you lost your biggest client for 60 days, and patch the weakest point.
Solid.priorityWhyItMatters: A concrete scenario test finds gaps a general sense of 'we'd probably be okay' misses.

Strength.headline: You're prepared to absorb setbacks
Strength.description: A financial and operational cushion protects the value you've built and gives you the freedom to weather a setback without everything falling apart.
Strength.priorityAction: Formally review your reserve and contingency plan annually so it keeps pace as the business grows.
Strength.priorityWhyItMatters: A cushion sized for today's business can quietly become insufficient as revenue and costs grow — a scheduled review keeps it real.

scoreInterpretationThresholds.text: At {score}/100, your business is performing strongly across most of what matters for its value and your freedom. This is a strong foundation to build on, and this report highlights the single dimension with the most room to grow.

At {score}/100, your business has a solid foundation with a few clear areas holding it back. Addressing the constraint below is likely to have an outsized impact on both business value and your freedom.
At {score}/100, your business is developing but has meaningful gaps that are limiting its value and your freedom right now. These gaps are common and addressable.

At {score}/100, your business is carrying real risk across multiple dimensions, which is likely limiting both what it's worth and how much freedom it gives you. Focusing on the constraint below is the highest-leverage place to start.

At {score}/100, this is an early diagnostic, not a verdict — it flags where your business is most exposed right now so you can prioritize with intention. Start with the single biggest constraint identified below.
